summary: RE-TEST (iteration 2) of APOLLO THREAT LAB mobile Expo app on public preview (390x844 viewport). All 9 acceptance criteria from the review request PASS. All 10 home testIDs render; both default Setup required badges on malicious/suspicious cards show; Stop when idle produces the honest idle message ('No in-app test is currently running. Note: a link already handed to the Android browser cannot be cancelled...'); Safe Traffic + Suspicious Connection on web go Running -> Failed with the honest disclaimer and NO fabricated Apollo verdict; Malicious Domain unconfigured correctly reports 'Setup required'; Malicious Domain configured on web correctly reports Failed with the honest 'Native DNS module is not available in this runtime (Expo Go and the web preview do not include it). Install the built Android APK...' message - FIX #1 validated end-to-end. One-at-a-time enforcement verified: while Safe Traffic was Running, scenario-phishing exposed aria-disabled=true. History correctly records entries with status pill, time, duration, destination, honest outcome and run ID; history-share-button is present and pressable (web returns a graceful 'Share is not supported in this browser' toast with no crash) - FIX #2 non-crash confirmed. Clear flow via modal (clear-confirm-modal / clear-cancel-button / clear-confirm-button) works and history-empty appears after confirm. Settings: all 5 settings-input-* fields render; saving valid maliciousDomain+suspiciousUrl removes both Setup required badges on Home; settings-reset-button clears optional fields; settings-back-button navigates back. NOTE: Default Redirect scenario legitimately shows 'Completed' on web because the default redirectUrl 'https://httpbin.org/get' responds with 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' and the fetch GENUINELY succeeds (HTTP 200, final URL recorded from the real network response). This is NOT fabricated - the honest disclaimer 'This is a network result only - it is not evidence that Apollo allowed or blocked anything. Verify Apollo separately in the Apollo app.' is still appended. HONESTY CONTRACT fully upheld across every scenario tested.
critical_code_review_comments: FIX #1 (abort-aware DNS) validated via UI: configured Malicious Domain on web honestly reports native DNS unavailable Failed with the correct Expo Go/web preview message instead of hanging or fabricating a Completed verdict.

FIX #2 (report redaction) is unit-tested in the Jest suite (query params + IP addresses stripped). On web the Share action degrades gracefully to a 'Share is not supported in this browser' toast - button present, pressable, non-crashing.

No deprecated Expo packages (expo-av/expo-barcode-scanner/expo-background-fetch) detected. All reference files <320 lines, pure RN components with Text wrapping, StyleSheet.create, and testID coverage. EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL correctly sourced from env; no hardcoded URLs.
